summary: Earth Jukebox is a browser-based web application that converts NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visual frames into real-time, multi-sensory audio soundscapes. By decoding pixel colours from NASA imagery colour bars into data values, it maps climate metrics to pitch, volume, stereo pan, and tempo. This directly addresses "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge by letting users hear climate trends, regional anomalies, and time-lapses live. Built with an accessibility-first design—featuring screen-reader support, keyboard navigation, and haptic feedback—it unlocks complex Earth science for blind, low-vision, and colour-blind learners, making climate data engaging and intuitive for everyone.
details:
​Earth Jukebox is a browser-based application that translates complex NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visual frames into real-time, multi-sensory audio soundscapes. By inverting colour bars into data values and mapping them to pitch, volume, stereo panning, and tempo, Earth Jukebox lets users hear climate trends, anomalies, and time-lapses live. Built for accessibility, it empowers blind and low-vision learners, colour-blind users, and anyone seeking an engaging, hands-free way to explore our changing planet.

  • ​Data Sources: NASA Earth Information Center (EIC), NASA GIBS/Worldview imagery layers, and NASA Earthdata/GISS numeric series.
  • ​Key Features: Client-side Web Audio synthesis, real-time decoding via Web Workers, full keyboard/screen-reader accessibility, and interactive sweep/point/time-lapse listening modes.
